key_insight: Semantic dispersion among sibling reasoning actions predicts downstream redundancy, enabling search budgets to be set before expanding subtrees.
engineering_relevance: Uncertainty-aware allocation can reduce LLM tree-search inference costs while preserving comparable reasoning accuracy.
method: Separate candidate value from uncertainty: value selects promising paths, while uncertainty controls expansion breadth.
Estimate uncertainty from sibling semantic dispersion without additional model calls.
Apply uncertainty-aware pruning and budgeting, motivated by an entropy-estimation analysis.
evidence_signal: Across mathematical reasoning, logical reasoning, and planning benchmarks, UAA reports up to 90% lower token usage and up to 9× lower latency at comparable accuracy across four search algorithms and open- and closed-source LLMs.
watch_item: Budgeting depends on sibling dispersion reliably predicting downstream redundancy; the abstract does not establish when this proxy may fail.
paper_title: Uncertainty-Aware Budget Allocation for Efficient LLM Tree Search
